group.title: Sport and fitness
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A person who is good at sport and trains to take part in it.
examples: Olympic {athletes} train for many hours every day.
wrong: He’s a top athlete, so he has never done any sport.

words.meaning: The person who controls a game and makes sure players follow the rules.
examples: The {referee} blew the whistle to end the game.
wrong: The referee scored the winning goal for his team.

words.meaning: The person or team you play against in a game.
examples: She shook hands with her {opponent} after the match.
wrong: My opponent and I played on the same team and helped each other.

words.meaning: A competition with many players or teams and a series of games.
examples: Thirty-two teams took part in the {tournament}.
wrong: The tournament was a single game between two friends in the garden.

words.meaning: A competition to find the best player or team in a sport.
examples: They won the national {championship} last year.
wrong: The championship is a practice session where nobody wins.

words.meaning: A group of teams that play against each other during a season.
examples: Our team finished third in the {league}.
wrong: A league is the ball used in tennis.

words.meaning: A person who watches a sports event or show.
examples: Thousands of {spectators} filled the stadium.
wrong: The spectators played the whole match while the team watched.

words.meaning: A path or ring made for running or racing.
examples: The runners lined up on the {track}.
wrong: We swam ten lengths of the running track.

words.meaning: An area of grass where games such as soccer are played.
examples: The players ran onto the {pitch}.
wrong: We played the soccer match on the pitch in the swimming pool.

words.meaning: The person who makes sure the rules are followed in games like tennis and baseball.
examples: The {umpire} said the ball was out.
wrong: The umpire hit the ball over the net to win the point.

words.meaning: To win against someone in a game or fight.
examples: Our team {defeated} the champions 3-1.
wrong: We defeated them, so they won the game.

words.meaning: A result in which both teams or players have the same score.
examples: The game ended in a {tie}, two goals each.
wrong: It was a tie because one team scored five and the other scored none.

words.meaning: A prize, often a silver cup, given to the winner of a competition.
examples: The captain lifted the {trophy} above his head.
wrong: The losing team was given the trophy as a punishment.

words.meaning: The best result that anyone has ever achieved in a sport.
examples: She broke the world {record} for the 100 meters.
wrong: He set a new record by finishing last in the slowest time ever.

words.meaning: The short break between the two halves of a game.
examples: The players drank water at {halftime}.
wrong: At halftime, the game was completely over and the players went home.

words.meaning: An action in a game that is against the rules.
examples: The referee saw the {foul} and stopped the game.
wrong: It was a foul because he played fairly and kindly.

words.meaning: The leader of a sports team.
examples: The {captain} spoke to the team before the game.
wrong: The captain is the player who has no say in the team.

words.meaning: To do gentle exercise to get your body ready before sport.
examples: Always {warm up} before you go for a run.
wrong: We warmed up after the race by lying down and going to sleep.

words.meaning: To do slow, easy exercise after hard training so your body can relax.
examples: After the race, we walked slowly to {cool down}.
wrong: She cooled down by sprinting as fast as she could.

words.meaning: To make your arms, legs or body as long as possible to loosen your muscles.
examples: He {stretched} his legs before the match.
wrong: I stretched my arms by holding them tightly against my body.

words.meaning: How healthy and strong your body is, especially from regular exercise.
examples: Swimming is great for your {fitness}.
wrong: His fitness improved because he stopped all exercise.

words.meaning: To run slowly and steadily for exercise.
examples: I {jog} in the park every morning.
wrong: She jogged to the station by sitting in a taxi.

words.meaning: To lose liquid through your skin because you are hot or working hard.
examples: We {sweated} a lot during the hot game.
wrong: He sweated because the room was freezing and he was resting.

words.meaning: To hurt a part of your body.
examples: He {injured} his knee during the match.
wrong: She injured her ankle, so it felt better than ever.

words.meaning: Doing a sport for fun, not as a paid job.
examples: He plays for an {amateur} soccer team on Sundays.
wrong: She’s an amateur player, so she earns millions from the game.

words.meaning: To take part in a race or competition and try to win.
examples: Over 200 runners will {compete} in the race.
wrong: She competed in the race by watching it on television.

words.meaning: The fact of winning a game, competition or fight.
examples: The fans celebrated the team’s {victory}.
wrong: After their victory, the team was sad that they had lost.

words.meaning: To start a soccer game by kicking the ball.
examples: The match {kicks off} at three o’clock.
wrong: The game kicked off at the end, when the players went home.

words.meaning: A running race of about 42 kilometers.
examples: She trained for months to run the {marathon}.
wrong: A marathon is a short race of about one hundred meters.

words.meaning: The best result a person has ever achieved in a sport.
examples: He ran a {personal best} of 41 minutes.
wrong: My personal best is my slowest time ever.

words.meaning: A period of physical exercise to keep fit.
examples: I did a 30-minute {workout} before breakfast.
wrong: My workout was an hour of lying on the sofa.

words.meaning: The quality of being physically strong.
examples: Lifting weights builds {strength}.
wrong: He had the strength of ten men, so he couldn’t lift the bag.

words.meaning: Breathing hard and fast after running or exercise.
examples: I was {out of breath} after climbing the stairs.
wrong: She was out of breath after sitting quietly in a chair.

words.meaning: Fit and healthy because you exercise.
examples: She runs every day to stay {in shape}.
wrong: He is in shape because he never moves from the sofa.

words.meaning: To raise heavy metal bars or objects to make your muscles stronger.
examples: He {lifts weights} at the gym three times a week.
wrong: She lifted weights by picking up a feather.

words.meaning: An exercise where you lie face down and push your body up with your arms.
examples: He did twenty {push-ups} before breakfast.
wrong: A push-up is an exercise you do while lying on your back and resting.

words.meaning: One complete trip around a track or along a pool.
examples: She ran four {laps} of the track.
wrong: One lap is half of the way around the track.

words.meaning: The line that marks the end of a race.
examples: He crossed the {finish line} in first place.
wrong: The runners started the race at the finish line.

words.meaning: To shout to show support or happiness.
examples: The crowd {cheered} when the team scored.
wrong: The fans cheered by sitting in total silence.

words.meaning: A player who comes on during a game to replace another player.
examples: The {substitute} scored two minutes after coming on.
wrong: The substitute played the full match from the very first minute.
